title: Anchor seat handoffs to repository state so staleness is visible
description:
A recorded seat handoff carries an ISO timestamp (scripts/seats/seat-handoff.mjs write) and the SessionStart injection reports its age in hours from file mtime (scripts/seats/seatContext.mjs). Nothing anchors it to repository state.

OBSERVED FAILURE (2026-09-07/08)
The claude-captain handoff was written at 2026-09-07T22:21:38Z. PR #536 merged at 03:26Z and PR #537 at 04:39Z the next day -- two integrations after the handoff was last touched. Its 'most useful next action' pointed at eshyra-jhpt children as open work that had partly landed. The successor reconciled from live state as required and lost nothing, so this is a cost-of-distrust defect, not a correctness one.

WHY THE EXHORTATIVE FIX IS THE WRONG ONE
The Claude Captain charter already says to record a handoff 'after an integration'. That instruction was in force and was not followed, and because the charter is personal and untracked, nothing could observe that it was skipped. Adding a stronger reminder repeats the approach that already failed.

PROPOSAL
Make staleness self-evident rather than writer-disciplined:
- seat-handoff.mjs write stamps the current origin/main (or main) SHA alongside the existing ISO timestamp comment.
- seatContext.mjs injection reports drift, e.g. 'recorded 6.4h ago at main 59d2ef9; main is now 2 commits ahead' -- and says so plainly when the recorded SHA is unreachable or the repo has moved to an unrelated history.
- A handoff with no recorded SHA (every existing one) degrades to today's behaviour rather than erroring.

The point is to tell the reader HOW MUCH to distrust the handoff. Today every handoff is equally suspect, so the reader re-derives everything from scratch every session; that cost is paid whether or not the handoff was stale.

ALSO IN SCOPE
docs/agent-captain-seats.md documents the handoff commands but not the recording discipline -- when a handoff should be written at all. A new occupant reading only repository authority learns the mechanism and none of the practice. Record the 'at meaningful boundaries, including after an integration' rule there, where it is durable and both seats can read it, rather than leaving it only in the untracked charters.

NON-GOALS
No tracked handoff content; handoffs stay personal, untracked, and never repository authority (docs/agent-captain-seats.md). No new seat state, no enforcement that blocks a session, no hook that refuses to start.

EVIDENCE
A test proving the injection reports drift for a handoff recorded at an older SHA, AND -- the control that matters -- that a handoff recorded at current main reports no drift. A SHA-less handoff still injects exactly as it does today.
close_reason:
NOT A DEFECT -- closed on corrected facts. The premise was wrong.

I filed this after observing that PRs #536 and #537 merged AFTER the claude-captain handoff was recorded (2026-09-07T22:21:38Z), and concluded a predecessor had skipped the charter's 'record a handoff after an integration' instruction. It had not. That work belonged to CODEX-CAPTAIN, which recorded its own handoff at 2026-09-08T03:27:48Z -- one minute after #536 merged -- explicitly noting 'PR #536 has crossed the merge boundary' and naming eshyra-jhpt.2.5 as the next unfinished question, which is what #537 then delivered.

Handoffs are per-seat by design (docs/agent-captain-seats.md: '<git common dir>/eshyra-seats/<seat>/handoff.md'). Each seat's file correctly described that seat's work. Neither seat skipped anything, and cross-seat awareness is supposed to come from Beads and Git -- which is where the successor got it, so the system worked as designed.

The proposed fix rested entirely on the false premise. The residual observation -- that the injection reports age in hours without anchoring to repository state -- is real but not worth acting on: reconciling from live state is unconditional, so knowing that main moved would not change any required behaviour. Recoverable from this note if anyone later disagrees.

The actual error was mine, and it is worth naming because it is a repeatable one: I treated my own inference from a timestamp comparison as a verified fact, without checking the obvious alternative explanation sitting one directory over. The seat charter's rule that a handoff is a set of leads to check applies to conclusions ABOUT handoffs too.
